attempted_claim: Let K=K(7,D) be a one-missing-digit set with |D|=6 covered by He-Liao arXiv:2602.01307 Theorem 1.5(2) (delta=dim_H K=log 6/log 7, mu=H^delta|_K/H^delta(K) with delta*dim_{l^1} mu>1/2), alpha>1 the constant from that theorem, theta in R\Z, tau in (1,alpha), psi_tau(q)=q^{-tau}, s(tau)=delta+2/(1+tau)-1, W_1(psi,theta)={x in [0,1]:||qx-theta||<psi(q) for infinitely many q}. Prove H^{s(tau)}(K cap W_1(psi_tau,theta))=H^{s(tau)}(K) (hence infinite), so dim_H=s(tau); i.e. H^s=0 for s>s(tau) and infinite for s<=s(tau) at fixed tau.
decisive_failure: This NO_RESULT reflects a one-hour lane with a single base paper (He-Liao v2) and bounded computation only; it does not prove the inhomogeneous critical-exponent law false, only that no credible route from the admitted base reaches it here. A future proof would need a genuinely new inhomogeneous small-scale estimate replacing the homogeneous simplex input, which lies beyond this lane's scope and resources.
